about: What /impact needs to model a datacenter (docs/methods/forecast.md, the datacenter sections), read by chain 740 (lab-desktop window 3) on 26 November 2026 from public documents, each value beside the words it comes from. `request` is the row of runs/c740/probe/probe.csv on lab-desktop. warehouse/forecast/datacenter_rules_check.py --verify-reads checks every quote against the kept text. A state not under `states` has no datacenter rule read: its exemption, property and electricity lines are blank with the reason.

split.words: JLARC, Data Centers in Virginia 2024, Appendix D, Table D-1: the initial capital spending of the datacenters using Virginia's exemption, 2021 to 2023, as VEDP collected it: land acquisition 6.1 percent, building and site improvements 19.6 percent, exempt equipment or software 68.2 percent, other 6.1 percent. "The percentages of spending by capital spending category are consistent with other research."

refresh.quote: Data center equipment is typically replaced every five years
refresh.words: JLARC, Data Centers in Virginia 2024, page 18: "Data center equipment is typically replaced every five years, which resets the depreciation schedule." The tool buys the equipment again at its first cost, in 2025 dollars, every that many operating years.

build.quote: data center building usually takes about 12 to 18 months
build.words: JLARC, Data Centers in Virginia 2024, page 14: "Construction of an individual data center building usually takes about 12 to 18 months, and it can take five or more years to fully build out a campus." The default is 18 months in whole years (2); a campus built in phases is the reader's longer figure.

life.words: A choice of horizon, not a sourced life: no public document read states a datacenter's operating life. 20 years is the initial term of Louisiana's exemption agreement (R.S. 47:305.73(B)(3)(b)). The reader sets the horizon.

mn.words: Minnesota only: the Carl Vinson Institute of Government's IMPLAN analysis (2023 data) for Minnesota's Legislative Budget Office, Tax Expenditure Evaluation: Minnesota Data Center Equipment Exemption (December 2025): Table 3, the economic impact of USD 346.8 million of direct construction output in 2013; Table 4, of USD 58.8 million of direct operations output in 2024 (677 permanent jobs). The tool applies its ratios of indirect and induced to direct jobs and labor income to the reader's on-site jobs and earnings.

ga.words: Georgia only: the Carl Vinson Institute of Government's IMPLAN analysis (2023 data) for the state auditor's evaluation of the data center exemption, statewide, 2025: Table 3, the economic impact of USD 3.3 billion of direct construction output; Table 4, of USD 715 million of direct operations output (1,873 permanent jobs). The tool applies its ratios of indirect and induced to direct jobs and labor income to the reader's on-site jobs and earnings. Its construction is "the building shell and its accompanying equipment", servers adjusted for leakage.

va.words: Virginia only: the Weldon Cooper Center's IMPLAN analysis for JLARC (2022 IMPLAN data, the data center sector customized: electricity 40 percent of operating spending, labor 15 percent), statewide annual averages of fiscal years 2021 to 2023 (Appendix D, Tables D-3 and D-5). The tool applies its ratios of indirect and induced to direct jobs and earnings to the reader's on-site jobs and earnings. JLARC's direct construction jobs include about 7,000 IT workers making and installing equipment beside 28,000 construction workers; its direct operating jobs are half of what datacenters reported to VEDP (the other half are contractors, counted as indirect).

sales_exemption.quote: Beginning July 1, 2010, and ending June 30, 2035, except as provided in subdivision 19, computer equipment or enabling software purchased or leased for the processing, storage, retrieval, or communication of data, including but not limited to servers, routers, connections, and other enabling hardware, including chillers and backup generators used or to be used in the operation of the equipment exempted in this paragraph
sales_exemption.tip: Virginia (Code 58.1-609.3(18)): computer equipment and enabling software, "including chillers and backup generators", are exempt through 30 June 2035 for a datacenter with "a new capital investment ... of at least $150 million" and "at least 50 new jobs" paying "at least one and one-half times the prevailing average wage in that locality" (10 jobs and $70 million in a distressed locality); not "general building improvements or other fixtures". The tool applies it when the investment and the permanent jobs meet the thresholds (the wage test is not checked), to equipment bought through 2034 (whole years: 2035's purchases are taxed). Subdivision 19 extends it to 2040 or 2050 for an operator investing $35 billion or $100 billion: not modeled.

property.quote: Computer equipment and peripherals used in a data center.
property.tip: Virginia: a datacenter's computer equipment and peripherals are their own class of tangible personal property for local taxation (Code 58.1-3506(A)(43)), each locality setting its rate and valuing it "by means of a percentage or percentages of original cost"; its fixtures (generators, substations, chillers, HVAC) are real property assessed "using the cost approach" (58.1-3295.3). Both rates are the locality's: none is held statewide. The tool applies the reader's rates to the building and the equipment at their cost, an upper bound where the locality depreciates.

electricity.quote: Each consumer of electricity in the Commonwealth shall pay electric utility consumption tax on all electricity consumed per month in excess of 50,000 kWh at the rate of $0.000875 per kWh
electricity.tip: Virginia's electric utility consumption tax (Code 58.1-2900), on each consumer's kWh a month: $0.001595 a kWh to 2,500, $0.001085 to 50,000, $0.000875 above (the state, special regulatory and local shares together). The tool takes a twelfth of the year's MWh as each month's. The local consumer utility tax (58.1-3812 on) is not read and not included.

sales_exemption.quote: the data center facility operator shall provide a sworn attestation that the project will create a minimum of fifty new direct, permanent jobs in Louisiana and intends to expend at least two hundred million dollars in new capital investment in Louisiana on or after July 1, 2024, and before July 1, 2029.
sales_exemption.tip: Louisiana (R.S. 47:305.73): state and local sales and use taxes "shall not apply" to an approved datacenter's equipment and to its "costs of construction and building materials", engineering, design, labor and installation, for a facility that attests to "a minimum of fifty new direct, permanent jobs" and "at least two hundred million dollars in new capital investment" before 1 July 2029; the agreement's "initial term of twenty years" may be renewed "for an additional ten years" at LED's discretion (not assumed). The tool applies it when the permanent jobs and the investment spent in whole years before 2029 meet the thresholds, for 20 years from the first construction year, to the equipment and, where the reader gives the building's taxable share, to the building.

property.tip: Louisiana (Constitution article VII, section 18): land and improvements are assessed at 10 percent of fair market value and other property at 15 percent; the millages are each parish's and taxing district's (none held statewide). The tool assesses the building at 10 percent and the equipment at 15 percent of their cost (no depreciation table is read: an upper bound) and applies the reader's rate. A payment in lieu agreed with a parish is not a statute: the abatement input is its place.

property.quote: Except for the taxable personal property enumerated below,
property.tip: Minnesota (Statutes 272.02, subdivision 9): all personal property is exempt except that enumerated (an electric generating, transmission or distribution system's, pipelines', railroad docks', leaseholds', manufactured homes' and flight property), so a datacenter's equipment owes no property tax. The building is taxed on its market value by class rates the ERW does not hold: the tool takes the building at its cost and the reader's effective rate, an upper bound.

sales_exemption.quote: where the total cost of construction or refurbishment, investment in enterprise information technology equipment, and computer software is at least $30,000,000 within a 48-month period
sales_exemption.tip: Minnesota (Statutes 297A.68, subd. 42): enterprise information technology equipment and software for a qualified data center (25,000 square feet and "at least $30,000,000 within a 48-month period" of construction, equipment and software; $250,000,000 for a large-scale one) are exempt, the tax collected "as if the rate under section 297A.62, subdivision 1, applied, and then refunded", for purchases "within 35 years" of the first, for centers certified "before July 1, 2042". The tool applies it at the state's rate only (local sales taxes are not named), for 35 years from the first construction year, when the investment meets USD 30 million; the square footage is not checked.

property.quote: (e) All other real property not herein provided for shall be taxed on an assessment equal to six percent of the fair market value of such property.

equipment.quote: all other personal property must be taxed on an assessment of ten and one-half percent of fair market value of the property

property.tip: South Carolina (Code 12-43-220): real property not otherwise classed is assessed at 6 percent of fair market value (e), and other personal property at 10.5 percent (f). The tool assesses the building at 6 percent and the equipment at 10.5 percent of their cost (no depreciation table is read: an upper bound) and applies the reader's rate. A fee in lieu of tax agreement with a county is an agreement, not a statute's rate: the abatement input is its place.

sales_exemption.quote: where a taxpayer invests at least fifty million dollars in real or personal property or both over a five year period
sales_exemption.tip: South Carolina (Code 12-36-2120(79)): computers, computer equipment and software used within a certified datacenter, and its electricity, are exempt where a taxpayer "invests at least fifty million dollars" over five years (75 million for several) and "creates and maintains at least twenty-five full-time jobs" at 150 percent of per capita income; a datacenter certified "prior to January 1, 2032" keeps it "for an additional ten year period". The tool applies it to the equipment through 2041 for a project starting before 2032; the electricity part needs a price the tool does not hold; the wage test is not checked.

property.quote: (c)  For real property in subclass (3), thirty-two percent.

personal.quote: the assessor shall annually assess all personal property at thirty-three and one-third percent of its true value in money

subclass.quote: all real property used directly or indirectly for any commercial, mining, industrial, manufacturing, trade, professional, business, or similar purpose

property.tip: Missouri (RSMo 137.115, with the subclasses of 137.016): real property used for commercial, industrial or business purposes (subclass 3) is assessed at 32 percent of true value, and personal property at 33 and one-third percent. The tool assesses the building at 32 percent and the equipment at one third of their cost (no depreciation table is read: an upper bound) and applies the reader's rate.

sales_exemption.quote: The new facility project investment is at least twenty-five million dollars during a period of up to thirty-six consecutive months
sales_exemption.tip: Missouri (RSMo 144.810): a new data storage center investing "at least twenty-five million dollars" in 36 months with "at least ten new jobs" at 150 percent of the county average wage is exempt from 100 percent of state and local sales and use taxes on its utilities, "machinery, equipment, and computers" and construction materials, for up to fifteen years, "limited to the net fiscal benefit of the state calculated over a ten-year period". The tool applies it for 15 years to the equipment and the building's taxable share; the net fiscal benefit cap (the Department's REMI model) is not modeled, so the forgone tax is an upper bound.

property.quote: property subject to taxation must be assessed at 35 percent of its taxable value.
property.tip: Nevada (NRS 361.225): all property subject to taxation is assessed at 35 percent of its taxable value. The tool assesses the building and the equipment at 35 percent of their cost (no depreciation table is read: an upper bound) and applies the reader's rate; an abatement the Office of Economic Development approves goes in the abatement input.

sales_exemption.quote: a cumulative capital investment of at least $25,000,000 in capital assets that will be used or located at the data center

terms.quote: Sales and use tax abatement reducing the rate to 2% for 10 or 20 years - requires the Governor's Office of Economic Development Board to approve a reduction to 2% by a two-thirds vote

sales_exemption.tip: Nevada (NRS 360.754): the Office of Economic Development may approve a partial abatement of the property and sales taxes on a new or expanded data center, for up to 10 years with 10 Nevada employees and "a cumulative capital investment of at least $25,000,000", or up to 20 years with 50 employees and $100,000,000, among other conditions. Its summary sheet (2025): 75 percent of the personal property tax, and the sales and use tax reduced to 2 percent, "by a two-thirds vote" of its Board, at wages of at least the statewide average. An approval, not a statute's rate: the tool applies none (the abatement input carries an approved property abatement; the sales tax rate input takes 2 for an approved reduction).

property.quote: North Dakota exempts all personal property from property taxation except that of certain oil and gas refineries and utilities.
property.tip: North Dakota (the Office of State Tax Commissioner, citing Century Code 57-02-04 and 57-02-08): "North Dakota exempts all personal property from property taxation except that of certain oil and gas refineries and utilities", so a datacenter's equipment owes none. The building's assessment ratio is not read: the tool takes it at cost and the reader's rate, an upper bound.

sales_exemption.quote: Gross receipts from sales of enterprise information technology equipment and computer software purchased for use by a qualifying business in a qualified data center are exempt from the tax imposed by this chapter.
sales_exemption.tip: North Dakota (Century Code 57-39.2-04.17): enterprise information technology equipment and software in a qualified data center (15,000 square feet or more, built or refurbished after 2020, certified by the tax commissioner) are exempt, replacements included; no investment, jobs or end date is set. The tool applies it to the equipment; the square footage and the certification are not checked.

sales_exemption.quote: for a data center located in any other area of the State, invested at least $5,000,000 in qualified data center personal property and created at least five qualified positions
sales_exemption.tip: Maryland (Tax-General 11-239): qualified data center personal property (computer equipment, HVAC and cooling, electrical equipment) is exempt where the operator has "invested at least $5,000,000" in it and "created at least five qualified positions" ($2,000,000 in a Tier I area or opportunity zone); the certificate is renewed yearly for up to 10 years, or 20 with "at least $250,000,000". The tool applies it to the equipment for 10 years from the first construction year, 20 with USD 250 million; the Tier I threshold is not modeled.

sales_exemption.quote: the data center's owners and tenants must make a cumulative capital investment of $150 million or more for the data center and the data center must have a critical IT load of 100 megawatts or higher
sales_exemption.tip: Florida (Statutes 212.08(5)(r)): data center property, "construction materials, component parts, machinery, equipment, computers, servers" and its electricity, is exempt where the owners and tenants make "a cumulative capital investment of $150 million or more" and the center has "a critical IT load of 100 megawatts or higher" within 5 years of the start of construction. The tool applies it to the equipment and the building's taxable share when the investment and the MW (read as critical IT load) meet the thresholds; the electricity part needs a price.

sales_exemption.quote: in amounts of at least two hundred fifty million dollars ($250,000,000) in the aggregate within the first five (5) years after commencement of construction and that it will create and maintain at least thirty (30) new jobs at the data center
sales_exemption.tip: Idaho (Code 63-3622VV): eligible server equipment and new data center facilities are exempt for a qualifying business entity that invests "at least two hundred fifty million dollars" within five years of the start of construction and creates "at least thirty (30) new jobs" paying the county's average weekly wage. The tool applies it to the equipment and the building's taxable share; the wage test is not checked.

property.quote: 17. Fifteen percent beginning from and after December 31, 2026.

class.quote: 13. Personal property that is devoted to any other commercial or industrial use, other than property that is specifically included in another class described in this article, and that is valued at full cash value.

property.tip: Arizona (A.R.S. 42-12001 and 42-15001): real and personal property devoted to commercial or industrial use is class one (subclasses 12 and 13), assessed at 15.5 percent of full cash value in 2026 and 15 percent from 2027. The tool assesses the building and the equipment at 15 percent of their cost (no depreciation table is read: an upper bound) and applies the reader's rate.

sales_exemption.quote: $50,000,000 of new investment, including costs of land, buildings, improvements, modular data centers and computer data center equipment, whether owned or leased or paid for pursuant to a right to use agreement, if the computer data center is located in a county with a population of more than eight hundred thousand persons.
sales_exemption.tip: Arizona (Revised Statutes 42-5061(B)(23) and 41-1519): computer data center equipment sold to the owner, operator or a qualified colocation tenant of a center certified by the Arizona Commerce Authority is exempt during the qualification period, "expiring at the end of the tenth full calendar year following the calendar year containing the effective date" (twentieth for a sustainable redevelopment project), where the center reaches $25,000,000 of new investment in a county of 800,000 people or fewer, or $50,000,000 in a larger county, within five years. The tool applies it to the equipment from the first construction year through the tenth full year after it, with USD 50 million (the county's population is not held: a center of 25 to 50 million in a smaller county qualifies and is not shown so).

sales_exemption.quote: at least seventy-five million dollars ($75,000,000) in private funds has been or will be invested by one or more owners, users, or tenants of the datacenter within five years
sales_exemption.tip: North Carolina (General Statutes 105-164.13(55a), with the definition of a qualifying datacenter in 105-164.3(201)): electricity and datacenter support equipment of a datacenter for which "at least seventy-five million dollars ($75,000,000) in private funds has been or will be invested" within five years are exempt, where the datacenter meets its tier's wage standard and provides health insurance. The tool applies it to the equipment; the electricity part needs a price; the wage standard is not checked.

property.quote: Exempts personal property from taxation beginning with assessments as of January 1, 2024
property.tip: Wisconsin (2023 Wisconsin Act 12, as the Department of Revenue describes it): personal property, locally assessed and state-assessed manufacturing property alike, is exempt from taxation from the assessments of 1 January 2024, so a datacenter's equipment owes none. The building's assessment is not read: the tool takes it at cost and the reader's rate, an upper bound.

sales_exemption.quote: For buildings located in a county having a population greater than 100,000, $150,000,000.
sales_exemption.tip: Wisconsin (Statutes 77.54(70), certified under 238.40): tangible personal property and items used exclusively for the development, construction, operation or replacement of a qualified data center, "including computer server equipment" and electricity, are exempt, for a center that reaches a qualified investment of $150,000,000 within 5 years of certification in a county above 100,000 people ($100,000,000 above 50,000; $50,000,000 otherwise). The tool applies it to the equipment and the building's taxable share with USD 150 million (the county's population is not held: smaller counties' lower thresholds are not shown); the electricity part needs a price.

sales_exemption.quote: amounts paid or charged for a purchase or lease made by a qualifying data center or an occupant of a qualifying data center of machinery, equipment, or normal operating repair or replacement parts

definition.quote: consists of one or more buildings that total 150,000 or more square feet;

sales_exemption.tip: Utah (Code 59-12-104(84), the version effective 1 July 2026, unchanged in this paragraph): machinery, equipment and repair or replacement parts bought by a "qualifying data center" or its occupant for its operation, with an economic life of a year or more, are exempt. A qualifying data center (59-12-102(111)) is a new operation constructed on or after 1 July 2016, in one or more buildings that total 150,000 square feet or more, owned or leased by its operator (or a company under common ownership) on land the operator owns or leases. The statute sets no investment, jobs or term: the tool applies the exemption to the equipment over the whole horizon. The floor area is not an input: a datacenter of less than 150,000 square feet does not qualify, and the reader turns the exemption off for it.

property.quote: Property identified as class seventeen property under this section, whether centrally or locally assessed, is taxed at 0.9% of its market value.
property.tip: Montana (Code 15-6-162): the land, improvements and equipment of a qualified data center (300,000 square feet and $150 million, or 25,000 square feet of new area and $50 million in 48 months) are class seventeen property, "taxed at 0.9% of its market value"; the mills are each district's. The tool takes 0.9 percent of the building's and the equipment's cost as the taxable value, with USD 50 million (the square footage is not checked), and applies the reader's rate (Montana's mills over 1,000, as a percent); below the threshold no rule is held.

property.quote: real property used for commercial and industrial purposes and buildings and other improvements located upon land devoted to agricultural use at 25%;

equipment.quote: Commercial and industrial machinery and equipment acquired by qualified purchase or lease made or entered into after June 30, 2006

property.tip: Kansas: real property used for commercial and industrial purposes is assessed at 25 percent (K.S.A. 79-1439), and commercial and industrial machinery and equipment bought after 30 June 2006 is exempt from all property taxes (K.S.A. 79-223). The tool assesses the building at 25 percent of its cost and the equipment at nothing, and applies the reader's rate.

sales_exemption.quote: A qualified firm that makes an investment in eligible data center costs in a qualified data center of at least $250,000,000 in the aggregate by the fifth year of operations and creates and maintains at least 20 new jobs at the qualified data center within two calendar years after the commencement of operations shall receive a sales tax exemption
sales_exemption.tip: Kansas (Statutes 74-50,332 and 79-3606(xxxx)): a qualified firm that invests "at least $250,000,000" in eligible data center costs by the fifth year of operations and creates "at least 20 new jobs" receives a sales tax exemption on eligible data center costs, data center equipment and construction purchases, under an agreement with the Secretary of Commerce. The tool applies it to the equipment and the building's taxable share; the exemption's duration (K.S.A. 74-50,333, not read) is not modeled, so it runs over the whole horizon here, an upper bound.

property.quote: failing to assess all property at 60% of its true and actual value.
property.tip: West Virginia (W. Va. Code 11-3-1(d), as the State Tax Commissioner's 2025 assessment ratio study states it): assessors assess all property at 60 percent of its true and actual value. The tool assesses the building and the equipment at 60 percent of their cost (no depreciation table is read: an upper bound) and applies the reader's rate. The High Impact Intelligence Center program is named in the governor's release but its law is not read (the code's host does not answer), so no datacenter rule of West Virginia is applied.

property.quote: Real Property Assessment Industrial and Commercial 40%

personal.quote: Personal Property Assessment Industrial and Commercial 30%

property.tip: Tennessee (the Comptroller of the Treasury's 2025 Tax Aggregate Report): industrial and commercial real property is assessed at 40 percent of value and industrial and commercial personal property at 30 percent. The tool assesses the building at 40 percent and the equipment at 30 percent of their cost (no depreciation table is read: an upper bound) and applies the reader's rate. No datacenter sales tax rule of Tennessee is read (www.tn.gov did not answer).

property.quote: The tax ratio is thirty-three and one-third percent (33-1/3%).
property.tip: New Mexico: taxable value is the property's value times the tax ratio, "thirty-three and one-third percent" (the Taxation and Revenue Department's general instructions, written for state-assessed property; the ratio is applied here to a datacenter's building and equipment as well). The tool takes one third of their cost (no depreciation table is read: an upper bound) and applies the reader's rate.

property.quote: In Georgia property is required to be assessed at 40% of the fair market value unless otherwise specified by law.
property.tip: Georgia (O.C.G.A. 48-5-7, as the Department of Revenue states it): property is assessed at 40 percent of fair market value by each county's Board of Tax Assessors. The tool assesses the building and the equipment at 40 percent of their cost (no depreciation table for a datacenter's equipment is read: at cost unless the reader types a schedule, an upper bound) and applies the reader's rate.

term.quote: (H) This paragraph shall stand repealed by operation of law on January 1, 2029 2032.

scope.quote: exempting a portion of construction materials and purchases of computer servers and related equipment from state and local sales and use taxes

sales_exemption.tip: Georgia (Code 48-8-3(68.1) as House Bill 1291 of 2022 amended it, read from the act as signed; the state auditor's evaluation, Table 1): high-technology data center equipment is exempt from state and local sales and use tax for a data center that creates 25 new quality jobs and USD 250 million of aggregate expenditures over any seven consecutive years in a county of more than 50,000 people (10 jobs and USD 75 million in a county of 30,001 to 50,000; 5 jobs and USD 25 million below), for equipment bought through 31 December 2031 (the act repeals the paragraph on 1 January 2032; the auditor's evaluation says the exemption was extended to 2033, which the act read does not say). New quality jobs pay at least 110 percent of the county's average wage (the auditor's words), which the tool does not test. The tool applies it to the equipment only (the auditor also names "a portion of construction materials", whose share is not read), with the largest county's threshold (county populations are not held), through 2031. The auditor estimates USD 474.2 million of state revenue forgone in FY2025.

sales_exemption.quote: At least $100,000,000 of new investment, on or after January 1, 2022, if the computer data center is located in a county with a population of more than 250,000 individuals and creates 45 new jobs.
sales_exemption.tip: Pennsylvania (Act 84 of 2016 as amended by Act 25 of 2021, the Department of Revenue's program guidelines and FAQ): computer data center equipment is exempt from the state's 6 percent sales and use tax (not from Allegheny's or Philadelphia's local tax) for a certified data center that creates "at least $100,000,000 of new investment" and 45 new jobs by the fourth anniversary in a county of more than 250,000 people ($75,000,000 and 25 jobs in a smaller county) and pays at least $1,000,000 of annual compensation after it; certification lasts "25 full calendar years following the year" of the application. The tool applies it at the state's rate, from the first construction year through the 25th year after it, with the larger county's threshold (county populations are not held).

sales_exemption.quote: For counties with a population of 100,000 or more, the minimum capital investment is $450,000,000.
sales_exemption.tip: Kentucky (KRS 139.499, with KRS 154.20-220 as House Bill 775 amended it, effective 27 June 2025, the Department of Revenue's words): data center equipment of a qualified data center project approved by the Kentucky Economic Development Finance Authority is exempt, where the project invests at least $450,000,000 in a county of 100,000 people or more ($100,000,000 in a county of 50,000 to 100,000; $25,000,000 below 50,000); building materials and electricity are excluded. The tool applies it to the equipment with the largest county's threshold (county populations are not held); its term is the agreement's, not stated, so it runs over the whole horizon here, an upper bound.

sales_exemption.quote: Be in a county with a population of 800,000 or more. This means it must be in King, Pierce, or Snohomish County.
sales_exemption.tip: Washington: the urban exemption (RCW 82.08.9861, as the Legislature's audit committee describes it in its 2026 review) exempts computer servers and power infrastructure of a data center in a county of 800,000 people or more (King, Pierce, Snohomish) with 20,000 square feet of server space and 1.5 MW of power; it "allowed no new exemptions after fiscal year 2028" and expires fully on 1 July 2038. The rural exemption (RCW 82.08.986) is not read: the Legislature's statute site disallows every automated read. The tool applies no exemption.

property.quote: Class II: 20% All property not otherwise classified.
property.tip: Alabama (the Department of Revenue's property tax page): property not otherwise classified (Class II) is assessed at 20 percent of its fair and reasonable market value. The tool assesses the building and the equipment at 20 percent of their cost (no depreciation table is read: an upper bound) and applies the reader's rate; a local Chapter 9B abatement goes in the abatement input.

sales_exemption.quote: Act 2026-573 makes updates to the requirements for data processing centers granted an abatement under Chapter 9B on or after January 1, 2027.

terms.quote: cities, counties, and public industrial authorities may grant tax abatements for new and expanding qualifying projects

sales_exemption.tip: Alabama (Code Title 40, Chapter 9B, as the Department of Revenue describes it): cities, counties and public industrial authorities "may grant" abatements of state sales and use taxes (all but a 0.75 percent state portion) and of property taxes. For a data processing center granted one before 1 January 2027: 10 years with up to $200 million invested in 10 years, 20 years above that and below $400 million, 30 years of property tax with more than $400 million in 20 years. Act 2026-573 changes the requirements for abatements granted from 1 January 2027, which the Department has not yet described. A local grant, not a statute's rate: the tool applies none (the abatement input carries a granted property abatement).

property.quote: Since at least 1955, County Assessors generally calculate taxes based on twenty percent of the current market value of the property
property.tip: Arkansas (A.C.A. 26-26-303, as the Assessment Coordination Division's 2025 annual report states it): county assessors calculate taxes on twenty percent of current market value, times the district's millage, for real and personal property. The tool assesses the building and the equipment at 20 percent of their cost (no depreciation table is read: an upper bound) and applies the reader's rate.

sales_exemption.quote: ($100,000,000) at the facility no later than five (5) years

scope.quote: following are exempt from the gross receipts tax levied by this chapter and

sales_exemption.tip: Arkansas (Code 26-52-456 as Act 548 of 2025 amended it, approved 10 April 2025, read from the act on arkleg.state.ar.us): data center equipment, eligible data center costs (land, buildings, site improvements, equipment, engineering and design), services and electricity of a qualified data center are exempt from the state's gross receipts and compensating use taxes. A qualified data center invests at least $100,000,000 at the facility within five years after construction begins, pays at least $1,000,000 a year of compensation in the state over its first two years of operation, is not a cryptocurrency miner, and has a positive cost-benefit analysis from the Arkansas Economic Development Commission (a qualified large data center: $2,000,000,000 within ten years and $3,000,000 of compensation). The act shows its changes as struck words: the $500,000,000 of the earlier law is struck, read from the lines drawn through it in the act's PDF. The tool applies it at the state's rate (the act names the state's taxes, not cities' and counties'), to the equipment and to the building's taxable share when typed, over the whole horizon (no term), with USD 100 million; the compensation and the Commission's analysis are not tested.

sales_exemption.quote: or $200 million if it is located elsewhere;

term.quote: Data centers must enter into tax incentive agreements with DECD, generally 20-year terms from the effective date;

extension.quote: Agreements may be extended to 30 years if the investment is at least $200 million and the data center is located in an enterprise zone or an opportunity zone or $400 million if it is located elsewhere

sales_exemption.tip: Connecticut (the Data Center Tax Incentive Program as the Department of Economic and Community Development describes it; the statute not read): a data center with a tax incentive agreement is exempt from sales and use tax on certain goods and services it buys and from property tax on certain real property and equipment, for agreements "generally 20-year terms", extendable to 30 years. The investment must be made by the fifth year: at least $50 million in an enterprise zone or a federal opportunity zone, $200 million elsewhere ($200 million and $400 million for 30 years). The tool applies the sales tax exemption to the equipment with the larger thresholds (zones are not held), from the first construction year for 20 years, or 30 with USD 400 million; the property exemption is the agreement's, with a host municipality fee, so it is left to the abatement input. The statute's host (cga.ct.gov) failed its certificate check, so the department's page is the source.

sales_exemption.quote: EOED will not be accepting applications from entities seeking certification to claim the Qualified Data Center Tax Exemption until further notice.

terms.quote: The applicant invests at least $50 million on "qualified data center costs" within 10 years of certification

sales_exemption.tip: Massachusetts (General Laws c. 64H, s. 6(zz), and 400 CMR 9.00, as the Executive Office of Economic Development describes them): a certified qualified data center is exempt for 20 years on data center equipment, software, electricity and construction costs, with at least 100,000 square feet, 100 jobs in the state within five years and $50 million of qualified costs within ten years. Since the administration's framework of 25 June 2026, "EOED will not be accepting applications from entities seeking certification to claim the Qualified Data Center Tax Exemption until further notice": a project now cannot be certified, so the tool applies no exemption.

sales_exemption.quote: Affiliates that will develop, own, and operate the facility, is not less than $250,000,000.00

jobs.quote: maintain a minimum of 30 Qualified New Jobs

term.quote: The time frame for this exemption is April 22, 2025 through December 31, 2050

certificates.quote: No new Certificates may be issued by the MSF after December 31, 2029.

sales_exemption.tip: Michigan (MCL 205.54ee and 205.94cc, as Public Acts 207 and 181 of 2024 amended them; the Michigan Strategic Fund's guidelines): data center equipment, including certain construction materials affixed to the building, of a certified enterprise data center is exempt from the state's 6 percent sales and use tax, with at least $250,000,000 of capital investment and 30 qualified new jobs paid 150 percent or more of the Prosperity Region's median wage, for purchases from 22 April 2025 through 31 December 2050 (2065 on a brownfield or a former power plant site); the Fund issues no new certificate after 2029, and a certified facility may take no state or local property tax benefit. The tool applies it to the equipment and to the building's taxable share when typed, through 2050, to a project starting before 2030; the wage condition is not tested, and the abatement input should stay at 0 for it.

sales_exemption.quote: signed an executive order ending access to tax incentives provided through the state's ImagiNE Nebraska Act for data centers
sales_exemption.tip: Nebraska: on 21 July 2026 the Governor "signed an executive order ending access to tax incentives provided through the state's ImagiNE Nebraska Act for data centers", prohibiting data center applications from being approved under the Act (the Governor's release). A project now cannot obtain them, so the tool applies no exemption.

property.quote: The taxable value is 35% of your property's appraised value.

equipment.quote: the vast majority of Ohio businesses no longer

property.tip: Ohio: real property's taxable value is 35 percent of its appraised value (the Department of Taxation's Property Tax Guide, January 2025); the tax on general businesses' tangible personal property (machinery and equipment) ended in 2009 ("for the first time in 163 years, the vast majority of Ohio businesses no longer faced a tax on tangible personal property", the Department's publication), continuing for telephone companies. The tool assesses the building at 35 percent of its cost and the equipment at nothing, and applies the reader's rate.

electricity.quote: All kilowatt hours over 15,000 distributed to each customer is subject to a rate of $.00363.

elective.quote: per kilowatt hour for each kilowatt hour in excess of 500 million kilowatt hours, distributed to a meter or location during the registration year

threshold.quote: must have consumed at least 45 million kilowatt hours of electricity in the previous

electricity.tip: Ohio's kilowatt-hour tax (the Department of Taxation's instructions for distributors' returns and its self-assessing purchaser application): on each customer's kWh in a 30-day billing period, $0.00465 on the first 2,000, $0.00419 on the next 13,000 and $0.00363 above 15,000; a commercial or industrial location using at least 45 million kWh a year may instead self-assess at $0.00257 a kWh on the first 500 million kWh of the year and $0.001832 above. The tool takes a twelfth of the year's MWh as each month's and, where the year reaches 45 million kWh, the lower of the two.

sales_exemption.quote: The Ohio Tax Credit Authority will stop accepting new data center tax exemption proposals after its currently scheduled meeting on Monday
sales_exemption.tip: Ohio: the Tax Credit Authority grants data centers sales and use tax exemptions case by case (the Governor's bulletin; the statute sits on codes.ohio.gov, which disallows every path to the ERW's reader). On 27 May 2026 the Governor directed the Authority "to pause consideration of any new data center tax exemption requests" while the General Assembly's Joint Data Center Committee studies data center growth; it "will stop accepting new data center tax exemption proposals" after its next meeting, and exemptions granted before stand. A project now cannot obtain one, so the tool applies no exemption.

sales_exemption.quote: Oklahoma imposes no minimum investment threshold, no job creation requirement, and no facility size requirement.

scope.quote: exempts the purchase of machinery and equipment by persons and establishments primarily engaged in computer services and data processing from state sales and use taxes.

power.quote: are eligible for sales tax exemption on equipment and machinery purchases (computers, servers, etc), but not on electric power.

sales_exemption.tip: Oklahoma (the Computer Services and Data Processing Tax Exemption, as the Incentive Evaluation Commission's draft evaluation of 30 September 2026 and the Department of Commerce describe it): machinery and equipment bought by an establishment primarily engaged in computer services and data processing are exempt from state sales and use taxes, where it derives at least 80 percent of its annual gross revenue from out-of-state buyers (Industrial Group 7374; 50 percent for 7372 and 7373); electric power is not exempt for these. "Oklahoma imposes no minimum investment threshold, no job creation requirement, and no facility size requirement", and the exemption has no duration limit. The tool applies it to the equipment at the state's rate over the whole horizon; the out-of-state revenue share is not tested. The statute's own host (oscn.net) disallows automated readers, so the evaluation is the source.

property.quote: (C) All other property, real and personal, nine and one-half percent (9.5%).

industrial.quote: (B) Property used for industrial purposes, eleven and one-half percent (11.5%);

property.tip: Wyoming (W.S. 39-11-101, title 39 on wyoleg.gov): taxable value is 11.5 percent of fair market value for property used for industrial purposes (manufacturing, processing materials, minerals, transforming property into new products) and 9.5 percent for all other property, real and personal. A datacenter is taken as other property: the building and the equipment at 9.5 percent of their cost (no depreciation table is read: an upper bound), times the reader's rate.

sales_exemption.quote: of not less than five million dollars ($5,000,000.00)

purchases.quote: of a data processing services center when the aggregate purchase of the qualifying equipment exceeds two million dollars ($2,000,000.00) in any calendar year;

jobs.quote: will create a number of jobs in Wyoming that is appropriate to the size and stage of development of the data processing services center as determined by the Wyoming business council

sales_exemption.tip: Wyoming (W.S. 39-15-105(a)(viii)(S), read from the statutes on wyoleg.gov): a data processing services center's computer equipment and software are exempt in a calendar year when its qualifying purchases exceed $2,000,000, with an initial capital investment in the state of not less than $5,000,000; its uninterruptible power supplies, generators and cooling equipment likewise with $50,000,000; and the Wyoming Business Council must certify that it creates jobs "appropriate to the size and stage of development" of the center. The tool applies it to the equipment with USD 5 million, over the whole horizon (no term), at the state's 4 percent (the exemption sits in the state's excise tax article; whether county taxes follow was not read); the yearly USD 2 million and the jobs certification are not tested.

property.quote: Most property is assessed at 33 1/3 percent of its fair market value.

cook.quote: Assessment levels range from 10 percent of market value for residential property to 25 percent of market value for commercial property.

property.tip: Illinois (the Department of Revenue's answer on assessment levels): most property is assessed at 33 1/3 percent of fair market value; Cook County assigns levels by class, 25 percent for commercial property. The tool assesses the building at one third of its cost (for Cook County, type the rate times 0.75 to give 25 percent). Whether a datacenter's equipment is taxed as property is not on the pages read: the tool applies the reader's rate to its cost, so leave the equipment's rate blank or 0 unless the county taxes it.

electricity.quote: $.00202 per kwh / in excess of 20 million kwhs
electricity.tip: Illinois' electricity excise tax (the Department of Revenue's excise rates page): delivering suppliers collect from each purchaser monthly $0.0033 a kWh on the first 2,000, falling by blocks to $0.00207 on the next 10 million and $0.00202 above 20 million kWh. A non-residential purchaser may instead self-assess 5.1 percent of its purchase price, which needs a price the tool does not hold, so the blocks are applied. The tool takes a twelfth of the year's MWh as each month's; municipal and cooperative systems' own rate (5 percent of charges or $0.0032 a kWh, the lesser) is not applied.

sales_exemption.quote: on June 5, 2026, DCEO will no longer process applications for the data center incentive program as of July 1, 2026.

terms.quote: New and existing data centers and their tenants collectively making a capital investment of at least $250 million over a 60-month period.

sales_exemption.tip: Illinois: the Data Center Investment program (the Department of Commerce and Economic Opportunity's page and its 2025 report to the General Assembly) exempted a certified data center from state and local sales and use taxes for up to 20 years, in five-year certificates, with "a capital investment of at least $250 million over a 60-month period" and 20 new jobs paid at least 120 percent of the county's median wage, under a memorandum of understanding with the Department. Per the Governor's directive of 5 June 2026 the Department "will no longer process applications for the data center incentive program as of July 1, 2026": a project announced now cannot be certified, so the tool applies no exemption. The statute's own host (ilga.gov) was not readable.

sales_exemption.quote: The Data Center Gross Retail and Use Tax Exemption provides a sales and use tax exemption on purchases of qualifying data center equipment and energy to operators of a qualified data center for a period not to exceed 25 years for data center investments of less than $750 million.
sales_exemption.tip: Indiana (Code 6-2.5-15, as the IEDC states it): qualifying data center equipment and energy are exempt "for a period not to exceed 25 years" below $750 million of investment, and "up to 50 years" above, as the IEDC awards it (Meta's Lebanon campus: a 35-year term for a minimum $1 billion in six years, request 88); local governments may also exempt enterprise information technology equipment from property tax with $25 million invested. The statute's minimum investments by county population sit in a code the ERW's reader cannot read (iga.in.gov builds it by script): the tool applies no exemption.

property.quote: All other real property, except for real property included in Class I or IV 15%

personal.quote: Personal property, except for motor vehicles and for personal property included in Class IV 15%

property.tip: Mississippi (the Department of Revenue's local property appraisal page): real property other than Class I or IV (Class II) and personal property other than motor vehicles and Class IV (Class III) are each assessed at 15 percent of true value. The tool assesses the building and the equipment at 15 percent of their cost (no depreciation table is read: an upper bound) and applies the reader's rate; a county's fee in lieu goes in the abatement input.

sales_exemption.quote: The Mississippi Development Authority has approved xAI for its Data Center Incentive, which provides a sales and use tax exemption for all computing and equipment software used by companies certified as data centers by the agency.
sales_exemption.tip: Mississippi: the Mississippi Development Authority's Data Center Incentive "provides a sales and use tax exemption for all computing and equipment software used by companies certified as data centers by the agency" (the governor's release on xAI, 8 January 2026). The statute's thresholds (Code 57-113-21) are not read from an official text: the tool applies no exemption. Counties and cities also agree fees in lieu of property tax (the abatement input).

property.quote: Personal property shall not be listed or assessed for taxation and is not subject to the
property.tip: Iowa (Code 427A.2, 2026): "Personal property shall not be listed or assessed for taxation and is not subject to the property tax", so a datacenter's equipment owes none. The building's assessment limitation for commercial property is not read: the tool takes the building at its cost and the reader's rate, an upper bound.

sales_exemption.quote: An eligible data center business must make a minimum investment in an Iowa physical location of $200 million within the first six years of operation in Iowa and meet other requirements described below.
sales_exemption.tip: Iowa (Code 423.3(95), as the Department of Revenue states it): with "a minimum investment in an Iowa physical location of $200 million within the first six years", qualifying computers and equipment are exempt permanently, and backup fuel and electricity for the first 10 years (in a city above 30,000) or 15 years, for property operating from 6 June 2025. The tool applies the equipment exemption when the investment meets the threshold; the electricity part needs a price the tool does not hold. Iowa's property tax on a datacenter is not read.

property.quote: and all other taxable property at its market value.

personal.quote: PERSONS AND PROPERTY LIABLE TO TAXATION

property.tip: New Hampshire (RSA 72:6, 72:7 and 75:1): "All real estate, whether improved or unimproved, shall be taxed", buildings "are taxable as real estate", and the selectmen appraise "all other taxable property at its market value". Chapter 72, "Persons and Property Liable to Taxation", names real estate, buildings, electric plants and pipe lines, and telecommunications poles and conduits; no section of it taxes a datacenter's computers, so the tool leaves the equipment untaxed (read from the chapter's list, not from a sentence that says so). The building is taken at its cost and the reader's rate (each town's), an upper bound. No sales tax rule is read for New Hampshire.

property.quote: FOR PROPERTY TAX YEARS COMMENCING ON OR AFTER JANUARY 1, 2027, THE VALUATION FOR ASSESSMENT FOR PERSONAL PROPERTY AND NONRESIDENTIAL REAL PROPERTY IS TWENTY-FIVE PERCENT OF THE ACTUAL VALUE THEREOF.
property.tip: Colorado (C.R.S. 39-1-104(1.9), as House Bill 24B-1001 enacted it in 2024): personal property and nonresidential real property are assessed at 27 percent of actual value for 2025, 26 percent for 2026 (25 for improved commercial property), and "FOR PROPERTY TAX YEARS COMMENCING ON OR AFTER JANUARY 1, 2027" at 25 percent. The tool assesses the building and the equipment at 25 percent of their cost in every operating year (no depreciation table is read: an upper bound) and applies the reader's rate. A later change to these percentages is not read. No sales tax rule is read for Colorado.
